whatIDo.title: What I do
whatIDo.body: Full-stack developer at TotalEnergies in France, I work on the frontend with React and TypeScript, on the backend with C# and SQL Server, and on Azure Cloud with Terraform and CI/CD pipelines in YAML on GitHub. I also write reusable and maintainable procedures that make it considerably easier to reproduce tasks already done.

learning.title: What I'm learning
learning.body: Deliberately expanding my skill set, from frontend toward cloud and systems thinking. Right now, I'm deepening my knowledge of infrastructure, CI/CD, concepts around Claude Code, and system design fundamentals. I'm still learning — and that's the whole point.

care.title: What I care about
care.body: Clarity and maintainability. After every task, I write a recap — what the problem was, what I changed, and where to start reading next time. Code that future-me (and teammates) can understand without a phone call.

think.title: How I think
think.body: Understand the business first, then break the problem down and ask the right questions — even the simplest ones. I use AI tools to move faster, but I still care about understanding the problem, checking the trade-offs, and knowing why the solution works. AI as a thinking partner, not autopilot.

inspectare.tagline: A PWA used by Vetting teams to manage and edit vessel audit reports, with offline access and data synchronization.
inspectare.why: A project developed within the TotalEnergies group at the request of the Vetting team to replace paper-based maritime inspection reports with a digital solution.
description: Development of a PWA for managing and editing vessel audit reports with offline mode and a standardized format for worker requests.
Implementation of data synchronization across multiple promises and integration of Service Workers for offline usage.
Management of complex front-end states with IndexedDB, speeding up data access.
Automation of deployments and Azure resource management via Terraform, reducing manual tasks by 90%.
Close collaboration with the DevOps team to set up CI/CD pipelines and secure cloud access.
inspectare.lesson: Learned more about PWA, Azure Cloud, React, LESS and teamwork — and I'm honestly glad I did.

kds.tagline: A digital screen system used in restaurants to manage kitchen orders
kds.why: A project I worked on during my apprenticeship year, which was commercialized before the end
description: Development of a real-time mobile application for restaurant order management.
Implementation of data synchronization via Firebase and real-time communication via TCP sockets.
Design of the user interface with Figma and compliance with ESLint standards.
Participation in the commercialization phase and delivery of two stable versions.
Independent work: code writing, testing, and debugging.
kds.lesson: Learned more about React Native, teamwork, and how to build a project from A to Z — and I'm honestly glad I did.

narrio.tagline: A small web application to support story progression
narrio.why: As one of the organizers of social events, I created this website to reduce the need for excessive paper printing
description: Most of the codebase was generated with Claude Code, while I focused on refinement, integration, and UI/UX improvements.
narrio.lesson: Learned how to work efficiently with Claude, discover what its limits are, and create a reusable SKILL.

mistakes.bad: Pushed to prod on a Friday

mistakes.learned: Suffered 3 months later. Documented everything after.

win_items.title: ✍️ Writing for clarity makes you think more clearly
win_items.summary: Vague writing is a symptom of vague thinking. The act of writing forces you to surface assumptions and fill in gaps you didn't know existed.
points: If you can't explain it in one clear sentence, you probably don't fully understand it yet.
Writing a design doc before coding exposes edge cases early — when they're cheap to fix.
Active voice + short sentences reduce cognitive load for the reader and force precision in the author.
The rubber-duck effect: writing to explain something to someone else reactivates your own understanding.
Docs written right after solving a problem are the most accurate — delay and you lose the 'why' behind decisions.
win_items.takeaway: Writing is thinking made visible. If the sentence is fuzzy, the idea behind it is too.

principles.note: A working solution teaches you more than the perfect plan ever could.
The best way to understand something is to build it, break it, and build it again.
Treat the codebase like your own house — you'll keep it clean if you know you're the one who lives in it.
